## Mixed models for the repeated visits {.unnumbered}

The cleaned data are in long format, with up to five rows per patient. Rows from the same patient are not independent, and chapter 2 showed it with the correlation between visits. A plain regression would treat them as independent. Ignoring the correlation gives the wrong standard errors, often too small for comparisons between arms.

A mixed model fixes this. It gives each patient their own starting level and, if needed, their own slope. It also uses every visit a patient attended. When dropout depends only on values we saw, called missing at random (MAR), this keeps the estimates valid. It does not fix dropout that depends on values we never saw. That is the next chapter.
